content.title: About
content.content: Syrup NFS (5026) is a thick sweet concentrate made from sugar syrup with added flavorings and stabilizers. It is used in culinary applications and beverages to provide sweetness and flavor without the need for large amounts of sugar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: NFS syrup is frequently used in professional bartending to craft cocktails.
It has a long shelf life due to its low water content.
The syrup is available in various flavor variants such as vanilla, caramel, and fruit blends.
Unlike granulated sugar, the syrup dissolves easily in cold liquids.
NFS syrup is produced without artificial colorings.

items.title: Quick source of energy
items.content: The syrup contains simple sugars that are rapidly absorbed, providing an immediate energy boost.

items.title: Convenient usage
items.content: Its viscous consistency allows precise dosing of sweetness without the risk of spilling granulated sugar.

items.title: Reduced dental abrasion
items.content: Compared to dry sugar, the syrup is less abrasive to tooth enamel when consumed in moderation.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive consumption can contribute to weight gain and elevated blood glucose levels.

items.title: Allergy to flavorings
items.content: Some individuals may react to the added aromatic compounds.

items.title: Not suitable for diabetics
items.content: The syrup has a high glycemic index and may cause rapid spikes in blood sugar.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add NFS syrup to tea, coffee, cocktails, desserts, sauces, and marinades. Typically 1–2 tablespoons per serving, adjustable to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in a tightly sealed container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For extended storage, keep refrigerated to prevent crystallization.
